notice: Provisional content for testing: independent review of clinical accuracy, source support, and duplication remains incomplete.

questions.stem: A patient has alveoli filled with inflammatory fluid. Which process is most directly impaired?

options.text: Movement of oxygen from alveoli into pulmonary blood
Movement of air through the nose

questions.rationale: Alveolar fluid increases the barrier to diffusion of oxygen into pulmonary blood.

questions.stem: An immobile patient aspirates gastric contents. Which complication is most directly associated with this event?
questions.rationale: Aspiration introduces material into the airway and increases pneumonia risk.

questions.stem: A patient has a positive TB test but no symptoms and is diagnosed with latent infection. Which description fits?

options.text: Organisms are contained and infection is inactive
The patient necessarily has disseminated TB

questions.rationale: Latent TB is inactive and asymptomatic; it is not spread to others.

questions.stem: During a severe asthma exacerbation, previously audible wheezing suddenly disappears while the patient becomes more distressed. What does this suggest?
questions.rationale: A silent chest with worsening distress can indicate critically diminished ventilation.

questions.stem: A patient with emphysema has damaged alveolar walls. How does this affect oxygen exchange?

options.text: It reduces available surface area for diffusion
It eliminates the need for ventilation

questions.rationale: Emphysema damages alveolar walls and reduces surface area available for exchange.

questions.stem: A patient develops a pneumothorax after a lung biopsy. What is present in the pleural space?
questions.rationale: A pneumothorax is air in the pleural space and may compress the lung.

questions.stem: A patient with a DVT suddenly develops dyspnea and chest pain. Why can a pulmonary embolus impair gas exchange?

options.text: Blood flow to ventilated alveoli is obstructed
The upper airway becomes narrowed by mucus

questions.rationale: Pulmonary vascular obstruction reduces perfusion available for gas exchange.

questions.stem: Which substance forms the mesh that stabilizes a clot?
questions.rationale: Fibrin forms a mesh that strengthens the platelet plug.

questions.stem: A patient is immobile after surgery. Which component of Virchow’s triad is most directly increased?
questions.rationale: Immobility promotes venous stasis, one component of Virchow’s triad.

questions.stem: A patient has thrombocytopenia. Which finding is especially consistent with a platelet problem?
questions.rationale: Petechiae are associated with platelet abnormalities such as thrombocytopenia.

questions.stem: A patient with disseminated intravascular coagulation develops oozing and organ ischemia. What explains the combination?

options.text: Widespread clotting consumes clotting components and produces bleeding
Red blood cell production alone causes the condition

questions.rationale: DIC produces systemic clotting and consumption of clotting components, causing bleeding.

questions.stem: A patient with iron deficiency anemia has microcytic, hypochromic red cells. Which pattern is expected?
questions.rationale: The worksheet associates iron deficiency with small, pale red cells and low MCV and MCHC.

questions.stem: Which packed red blood cell type is commonly identified as the universal emergency donor?
questions.rationale: O negative red cells lack A, B, and Rh D antigens; compatibility procedures still apply.

questions.stem: A patient develops fluid overload associated with a blood transfusion. Which reaction is described?
questions.rationale: TACO is transfusion-associated circulatory overload.

questions.stem: Which cell is associated with Hodgkin lymphoma?
questions.rationale: Reed-Sternberg cells are associated with Hodgkin lymphoma.

questions.stem: A patient with leukemia has anemia, infections, and bleeding. What underlying process can contribute to these findings?

options.text: Neoplastic cells crowd the marrow and impair normal cell production
Excess functional platelets replace all leukocytes
The disease affects only mature red cells
Bone marrow produces no abnormal white cells

questions.rationale: Leukemic proliferation in marrow can interfere with normal blood cell production.

questions.stem: A patient has marked proteinuria, foamy urine, and generalized edema. Which syndrome best fits?
questions.rationale: The worksheet associates nephrotic syndrome with massive proteinuria and generalized edema.

questions.stem: A patient has fever, chills, and costovertebral angle tenderness. Which infection is most consistent with these findings?
questions.rationale: Fever and costovertebral angle tenderness are findings associated with upper urinary tract infection.

questions.stem: A patient has a urinary outflow obstruction. What does hydronephrosis describe?

options.text: Dilation of the renal pelvis and calyces with urine
A decrease in bladder volume caused by cystitis
A blood clot in a pulmonary artery

questions.rationale: Obstructed outflow can cause urine-filled dilation of the renal collecting system.

questions.stem: A patient develops AKI after severe dehydration. Which category best describes the cause?
questions.rationale: Dehydration can reduce kidney perfusion and cause prerenal AKI.

questions.stem: A patient with advanced CKD develops anemia and fatigue. Which kidney function helps explain the anemia?
questions.rationale: Reduced kidney erythropoietin production contributes to anemia in advanced CKD.

questions.stem: Which structure acts as the semipermeable membrane in peritoneal dialysis?
questions.rationale: Peritoneal dialysis uses the peritoneal membrane for exchange with dialysate.

questions.stem: A patient leaks urine when coughing or laughing. Which type of incontinence is most consistent with this pattern?
questions.rationale: Stress incontinence occurs with increased intra-abdominal pressure, such as coughing or laughing.

questions.stem: Which processes contribute to narrowed airways during an asthma exacerbation? Select all that apply.
questions.rationale: Asthma involves bronchoconstriction, inflammation with edema, and increased mucus.

questions.stem: Which circumstances increase the risk of deep vein thrombosis? Select all that apply.
questions.rationale: The worksheet lists immobility, pregnancy, estrogen use, and heart failure as DVT risks.

questions.stem: Which findings support cystitis? Select all that apply.
questions.rationale: Dysuria, frequency, urgency, and lower abdominal pain are associated with cystitis; fever and CVA tenderness suggest upper tract involvement.

questions.stem: Which findings can occur with advanced chronic kidney disease? Select all that apply.
questions.rationale: Advanced CKD can reduce potassium and acid excretion, retain fluid, and decrease erythropoietin production.

questions.stem: Which findings are associated with active tuberculosis rather than asymptomatic latent infection? Select all that apply.
questions.rationale: Active TB may cause constitutional and respiratory symptoms; latent TB is asymptomatic.

questions.stem: Which factors can precipitate a sickle cell vaso-occlusive crisis? Select all that apply.
questions.rationale: The worksheet identifies dehydration, infection, cold exposure, and hypoxia as triggers for sickling and vaso-occlusion.

questions.stem: Match each cause of acute kidney injury to its category.
questions.rationale: Dehydration reduces perfusion, nephrotoxins injure kidney tissue, and obstruction impairs urine outflow.

questions.stem: Match each description with the anemia.

pairs.prompt: Low iron with small, pale red blood cells
Vitamin B12 deficiency with neurologic symptoms
Bone marrow failure affecting multiple cell lines

questions.rationale: Iron deficiency is microcytic and hypochromic; B12 deficiency may cause neurologic symptoms; aplastic anemia involves marrow failure.

questions.stem: Match each condition with what is present in the pleural space.
questions.rationale: Pneumothorax contains air, hemothorax contains blood, and empyema is infection in the pleural cavity.

questions.stem: Match each dialysis method with its characteristic.
questions.rationale: Peritoneal dialysis uses the peritoneum and carries a peritonitis risk; hemodialysis can use an AV fistula.

questions.stem: An older patient with pneumonia becomes newly confused and has a low oxygen saturation. What is a likely contributor to the change in mental status?
questions.rationale: Impaired gas exchange in pneumonia can cause hypoxemia and confusion.

questions.stem: A patient has infection involving a single pulmonary lobe. Which pneumonia distribution is described?
questions.rationale: Lobar pneumonia involves a single lung lobe.

questions.stem: A patient with previous latent tuberculosis becomes immunosuppressed and develops cough, fever, and weight loss. What process is most consistent?
questions.rationale: Latent TB can become active when immune defenses are suppressed.

questions.stem: A patient has a severe asthma attack that persists despite therapy. Which term describes this situation?
questions.rationale: Status asthmaticus is a persistent severe asthma attack that does not respond to therapy.

questions.stem: A patient with COPD has chronically low oxygen levels. Which blood finding can occur as a compensatory response?

options.text: Marked platelet consumption from DIC in every patient

questions.rationale: Chronic hypoxemia can stimulate red blood cell production and result in polycythemia.

questions.stem: A patient with COPD develops pulmonary hypertension. Which chamber must work harder to pump against this pressure?
questions.rationale: The right ventricle pumps into pulmonary circulation; increased pulmonary pressure raises its workload.

questions.stem: A patient with pneumonia develops infected fluid within the pleural cavity. Which complication does this describe?
questions.rationale: Empyema is infection in the pleural cavity and may occur adjacent to bacterial pneumonia.

questions.stem: A patient with a massive pulmonary embolism becomes hypotensive. Which mechanism can contribute?

options.text: Reduced blood flow through the lungs limits left-sided cardiac filling
Increased blood return to the left heart

questions.rationale: A massive embolus can obstruct pulmonary blood flow, reduce left ventricular filling, and impair systemic perfusion.

questions.stem: After a clot has served its purpose, which enzyme directly breaks down fibrin?
questions.rationale: Plasmin participates in fibrinolysis and breaks down the fibrin clot.

questions.stem: A patient with hemophilia A has a deficiency of which coagulation factor?
questions.rationale: The worksheet identifies hemophilia A as a factor VIII deficiency.

questions.stem: A patient develops disseminated intravascular coagulation after a serious obstetric complication. Why is urgent follow-up needed?

options.text: Widespread clotting and bleeding can occur together
The disorder affects urine flow only

questions.rationale: DIC can cause widespread clotting and bleeding due to consumption of platelets and clotting factors; obstetric complications are a risk.

questions.stem: For red blood cell transfusion, which ABO and Rh type is commonly described as the universal recipient?
questions.rationale: AB positive is commonly described as the universal red blood cell recipient; compatibility testing remains necessary.

questions.stem: Which type of leukemia is most common in children according to the worksheet?
questions.rationale: The worksheet identifies acute lymphocytic leukemia as the most common type in children.

questions.stem: A patient with chronic myeloid leukemia asks about a characteristic chromosome abnormality. Which is associated with CML?

options.text: An extra Y chromosome in every case

questions.rationale: The Philadelphia chromosome is associated with chronic myeloid leukemia.

questions.stem: A patient develops hematuria after a streptococcal infection. Which syndrome is consistent with the worksheet?
questions.rationale: The worksheet associates nephritic syndrome with hematuria and prior streptococcal infection.

questions.stem: A patient has sudden severe flank pain radiating toward the groin with possible hematuria. Which condition best fits?
questions.rationale: Renal colic from a urinary stone can cause severe flank or groin pain and hematuria.

questions.stem: A patient with benign prostatic hyperplasia develops urinary obstruction and rising creatinine. Which category of AKI is most consistent?
questions.rationale: BPH can obstruct urinary outflow, causing postrenal AKI.

questions.stem: A patient with advanced CKD has weak bones and low calcium. What mechanism contributes?

options.text: Reduced vitamin D activation decreases calcium absorption
Excess kidney activation of vitamin D in all patients
Improved calcium absorption eliminates PTH release
Loss of fibrin causes bone fractures

questions.rationale: Reduced renal vitamin D activation contributes to hypocalcemia and secondary bone changes.

questions.stem: A patient feels a sudden intense need to void and leaks before reaching the toilet. Which type of incontinence is described?
questions.rationale: Urge incontinence involves a sudden intense urge followed by involuntary urine loss.

questions.stem: A nurse explains breathing to a patient. Which statement describes ventilation?

options.text: Movement of air into and out of the lungs
Transfer of oxygen from alveoli into blood
Clot formation in a pulmonary vessel
Movement of urine through the ureters

questions.rationale: Ventilation is movement of air; gas exchange is transfer of gases between alveoli and blood.

questions.stem: A patient with dysphagia aspirates oral secretions. Why does this increase pneumonia risk?

options.text: Material containing organisms may enter the respiratory tract
The pleural cavity necessarily fills with air
All red blood cells become sickled

questions.rationale: Aspiration can introduce oral secretions into the lower respiratory tract.

questions.stem: A chest radiograph shows patchy areas of consolidation throughout both lungs. Which distribution does this suggest?
questions.rationale: The worksheet describes bronchopneumonia as diffuse, patchy consolidation in one or both lungs.

questions.stem: A patient develops tuberculosis involving the kidneys and meninges. Which complication describes this dissemination?
questions.rationale: Miliary tuberculosis can disseminate to organs beyond the lungs.

questions.stem: Which group has increased risk of tuberculosis exposure according to the worksheet?

options.text: People living in crowded correctional facilities
People with an ABO blood type of O
People with seasonal dry skin alone

questions.rationale: The worksheet identifies crowded living conditions, including prisons, as a TB exposure risk.

questions.stem: A patient develops coughing and wheezing after exposure to an inhaled allergen. Which type of asthma trigger is described?
questions.rationale: Extrinsic asthma triggers can involve inhaled antigens and type I hypersensitivity.

questions.stem: A patient with asthma has an exacerbation after cold-air exposure. Which trigger category best fits?
questions.rationale: Cold exposure is listed among intrinsic asthma triggers.

questions.stem: A patient has a genetic alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency. Which COPD component is associated with this risk?
questions.rationale: The worksheet identifies alpha-1 antitrypsin mutation as a cause of emphysema.

questions.stem: Why might a patient with COPD use pursed-lip breathing?

options.text: To help keep airways open during exhalation
To increase red blood cell destruction
To move urine past an obstruction

questions.rationale: Pursed-lip breathing helps with expiration in the presence of airflow limitation and air trapping.

questions.stem: A patient has a collection of blood in the pleural cavity after chest trauma. Which term describes it?
questions.rationale: Hemothorax is blood in the pleural space.

questions.stem: A patient with recent leg swelling suddenly becomes short of breath and anxious. Which prior finding raises concern for a pulmonary embolus?
questions.rationale: A DVT is a significant risk factor for pulmonary embolism.

questions.stem: A vessel is injured. What is the initial response that helps reduce blood loss?
questions.rationale: Vasoconstriction reduces flow at the site of injury and is an early step in hemostasis.

questions.stem: Which process pulls the edges of damaged tissue closer after clot formation?
questions.rationale: Clot retraction tightens the clot and draws injured tissue edges together.

questions.stem: A patient develops unilateral leg swelling, tenderness, and redness. Which condition should the nurse suspect?
questions.rationale: Unilateral edema, pain, and erythema are associated with DVT.

questions.stem: A patient with von Willebrand factor deficiency has difficulty with which early clotting step?
questions.rationale: Von Willebrand factor supports platelet adhesion during formation of the platelet plug.

questions.stem: A patient with sickle cell anemia has pallor and yellow sclera. Which combination best explains these findings?

options.text: Excess hemoglobin and no red-cell breakdown
Increased platelet production and dehydration alone
Excess oxygen diffusion and high hemoglobin

questions.rationale: Low hemoglobin contributes to pallor and hemolysis can contribute to jaundice.

questions.stem: A patient has aplastic anemia. Which combination reflects the potential effects of bone marrow failure?

options.text: Anemia, infection risk, and bleeding risk

questions.rationale: Marrow failure can reduce red cells, white cells, and platelets.

questions.stem: A patient has painless lymph node enlargement, night sweats, and weight loss. Which disorder is consistent with this group of findings?
questions.rationale: The worksheet lists painless lymphadenopathy and constitutional symptoms among lymphoma manifestations.

questions.stem: A patient with leukemia has a very high white blood cell count and signs of impaired pulmonary and cerebral circulation. Which complication should be considered?
questions.rationale: Leukostasis involves abnormal high leukocyte counts and impaired blood flow, particularly in pulmonary and cerebral circulation.

questions.stem: A patient with nephrotic syndrome has extensive protein loss in urine. Which urine appearance is commonly associated with this finding?

options.text: Urine containing air from the pleural cavity

questions.rationale: The worksheet associates massive proteinuria with foamy urine in nephrotic syndrome.

questions.stem: A patient with an indwelling catheter asks about infection risk. Which factor increases the risk of a hospital-acquired urinary tract infection?

options.text: An intact skin surface without instrumentation

questions.rationale: The worksheet identifies indwelling urinary catheters as a major hospital UTI risk.

questions.stem: A patient has recurrent stones associated with urinary tract infections. Which type is associated with this history in the worksheet?
questions.rationale: The worksheet associates struvite stones with urinary tract infections.

questions.stem: A patient with gout has a kidney stone. Which stone type is associated with gout in the worksheet?
questions.rationale: Uric acid stones are associated with gout and high-purine intake in the worksheet.

questions.stem: A patient develops kidney injury following a nephrotoxic medication. Which category of AKI fits?
questions.rationale: Nephrotoxic medications can directly injure kidney tissue and cause intrarenal AKI.

questions.stem: A patient with heart failure has reduced cardiac output and rising creatinine. Which type of AKI is most consistent?

options.text: Intrarenal from a stone in the bladder

questions.rationale: Reduced cardiac output can lower renal perfusion and produce prerenal AKI.

questions.stem: A patient with advanced CKD has elevated potassium. What kidney problem contributes?

options.text: Excessive potassium excretion in all cases

questions.rationale: Reduced excretion in advanced CKD can contribute to hyperkalemia.

questions.stem: A patient on peritoneal dialysis reports signs of abdominal infection. Which complication is associated with this treatment?
questions.rationale: Peritonitis is a recognized complication of peritoneal dialysis.

questions.stem: During hemodialysis a patient becomes lightheaded and hypotensive. Which treatment-related change may contribute?

options.text: Improved blood volume from no fluid exchange
Increased urine output in every patient
Increased clot retraction in the bladder

questions.rationale: Fluid shifts and removal during hemodialysis can contribute to hypotension.

questions.stem: A patient is immobilized after surgery. Which factors can increase pneumonia risk? Select all that apply.
questions.rationale: Immobility can impair secretion management and lung expansion and increase aspiration risk.

questions.stem: Which changes are associated with COPD in the worksheet? Select all that apply.

options.text: Fibrosis and thickening of bronchial walls

questions.rationale: COPD involves airway changes and mucus; emphysema also involves alveolar damage.

questions.stem: Which findings may occur with pulmonary embolism? Select all that apply.
questions.rationale: The worksheet lists chest pain, shortness of breath, tachycardia, anxiety, and restlessness as potential findings.

questions.stem: Which elements are part of Virchow’s triad? Select all that apply.
questions.rationale: Virchow’s triad consists of venous stasis, endothelial injury, and hypercoagulability.

questions.stem: Which manifestations may be associated with vitamin B12 deficiency in pernicious anemia? Select all that apply.

options.text: Microcytic hypochromic cells as the typical pattern

questions.rationale: The worksheet associates pernicious anemia with macrocytosis and neurologic findings such as paresthesias and ataxia.

questions.stem: Which findings may occur with a urinary stone? Select all that apply.
questions.rationale: The worksheet lists renal colic, nausea and vomiting, and possible hematuria among stone findings.

questions.stem: Which causes are classified as prerenal in the worksheet? Select all that apply.

options.text: Reduced cardiac output from heart failure
Reduced cardiac output after myocardial infarction

questions.rationale: Prerenal AKI involves reduced renal perfusion; BPH causes postrenal obstruction.

questions.stem: Which findings may result from uremia in advanced CKD? Select all that apply.
questions.rationale: The worksheet lists fatigue, gastrointestinal symptoms, weakness, confusion, and encephalopathy as uremic manifestations.

questions.stem: Which complications are associated with hemodialysis? Select all that apply.

options.text: Peritonitis as the defining hemodialysis complication

questions.rationale: The worksheet lists hypotension, infection, access thrombosis, and fluid or electrolyte shifts as hemodialysis complications.

questions.stem: Which findings are more consistent with a platelet-related bleeding problem than a deep joint bleed? Select all that apply.

options.text: Hemarthrosis as the distinguishing platelet finding
Normal platelet count in every case

questions.rationale: Petechiae, mucosal bleeding, and low platelet counts fit thrombocytopenia; hemarthrosis is characteristic of factor deficiencies.

questions.stem: Match each stage of hemostasis with its function.

targets.text: Reduces blood flow at the injury

questions.rationale: Hemostasis begins with vasoconstriction and platelet plug formation, followed by coagulation; fibrinolysis removes the clot.

questions.stem: Match each tuberculosis description with the corresponding form.

questions.rationale: Pulmonary hypertension increases right ventricular workload; chronic hypoxia can stimulate erythrocyte production.

questions.rationale: The worksheet associates struvite stones with UTIs, uric acid stones with gout, cystine stones with genetic causes, and calcium stones with hypercalcemia.

pairs.prompt: Leakage after a sudden strong need to void

questions.rationale: Stress incontinence occurs with increased abdominal pressure; urge incontinence follows a sudden compelling urge.

questions.stem: Which changes can contribute to bone complications in advanced CKD? Select all that apply.

options.text: Increased bone formation in every affected patient
Consistently increased renal vitamin D activation

questions.rationale: Reduced vitamin D activation can contribute to hypocalcemia, secondary PTH elevation, and bone loss.
questions.sourceReview: Provisional: course-source and clinical review incomplete

questions.stem: Which are potential complications of peritoneal dialysis listed in the worksheet? Select all that apply.

options.text: An AV graft thrombosis as the typical abdominal complication
AV fistula thrombosis as its abdominal access complication

questions.rationale: Peritoneal dialysis complications include peritonitis, catheter infection, hernias, and back pain.
questions.sourceReview: Provisional: course-source and clinical review incomplete

questions.stem: The nurse reviews access options for hemodialysis. Which are listed in the worksheet? Select all that apply.

options.text: Peritoneal dialysis catheter as the standard vascular hemodialysis access

questions.rationale: The worksheet lists an AV fistula, AV graft, and central line as hemodialysis access options.
questions.sourceReview: Provisional: course-source and clinical review incomplete

questions.stem: Which conditions are listed in the worksheet as potential causes of chronic kidney disease? Select all that apply.

options.text: A brief cough with no kidney injury

questions.rationale: Diabetes, hypertension, and irreversible AKI are listed as potential CKD causes.
questions.sourceReview: Provisional: course-source and clinical review incomplete

questions.stem: A patient develops a pleural effusion during pneumonia. The fluid contains protein and inflammatory cells. Which mechanism from the worksheet best explains an exudative effusion?

options.text: Reduced hydrostatic pressure keeps all fluid inside vessels
Red blood cells are unable to make hemoglobin
Reduced bile production creates air in the pleural cavity

questions.rationale: Inflammation increases permeability and can produce an exudative pleural effusion containing protein and white blood cells.
questions.sourceReview: Provisional: course-source and clinical review incomplete

questions.stem: A patient using estrogen-containing oral contraceptives has been immobile during a long trip. Which two parts of Virchow's triad do these factors most directly represent?
questions.rationale: The worksheet associates estrogen with hypercoagulability and immobility with venous stasis.
questions.sourceReview: Provisional: course-source and clinical review incomplete

questions.stem: True or false: A positive tuberculosis skin test can occur with either active or latent tuberculosis.
questions.rationale: The worksheet identifies a positive skin test as possible in both active and latent TB.
questions.sourceReview: Provisional: course-source and clinical review incomplete

questions.stem: A nurse explains the difference between ventilation and gas exchange. Which statement describes gas exchange?

options.text: Oxygen and carbon dioxide move between the alveoli and pulmonary blood
Air moves into and out of the lungs
Urine moves from the kidneys to the bladder
Platelets aggregate at an injured vessel

questions.rationale: Gas exchange is the transfer of oxygen and carbon dioxide between alveoli and pulmonary capillary blood.

questions.stem: For emergency red blood cell transfusion, what characteristic makes O-negative cells broadly compatible?

options.text: They lack A, B, and Rh D antigens
They carry both A and B antigens
They have every possible platelet antigen

questions.rationale: O-negative red cells lack A, B, and Rh D antigens; standard compatibility procedures still apply.
questions.sourceReview: Provisional: course-source and clinical review incomplete

questions.stem: A patient with leukemia has frequent infections despite a high white blood cell count. What is one explanation?

options.text: Many leukemic white cells are abnormal and do not function normally
The count measures only red cells

questions.rationale: Leukemic proliferation may produce abnormal, ineffective white blood cells and interfere with normal marrow function.
questions.sourceReview: Provisional: course-source and clinical review incomplete

questions.stem: A patient leaks urine when laughing and lifting. Which mechanism is most consistent?

options.text: Increased abdominal pressure overcomes weakened pelvic support
All urine leakage is caused by kidney stones
The patient has an absolute lack of bladder sensation

questions.rationale: Stress incontinence occurs with increased intra-abdominal pressure, often in the setting of weakened pelvic floor support.
